title: Pattern-Like M5 Common Definitions
description: Vocabulary introduced by the M5 constrained-model publisher. Anything unchanged from M0 is referenced by absolute $id from https://patternlike.app/contracts/m0/common.schema.json, and the generic reading vocabulary M3 introduced and M5 does not supersede — policy versions, revision counters, suppression classes, provenance sources — is referenced from https://patternlike.app/contracts/m3/common.schema.json. M5 supersedes the daily-reading FAMILY (the reading artifact, its evidence graph, and its generation command), not those two packages wholesale, so restating their enums here would create a second copy that can drift. Normative sources: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-10-openai-daily-reading-publisher-design.md.

schemaVersion.description: M5 contract package version. M0 stays at 0.2.0 and M3 at 0.3.0; both are byte-frozen.

outputSchemaName.description: Pinned structured output schema for constrained-model publication. Defined by daily-reading.schema.json in this package. A frozen command names this value, so a schema change is a new name rather than a reinterpretation of the old one.

assemblyMode.description: The only assembly mode M5 produces. deterministic remains the M3 value, and a v5 artifact can never claim it.

dailySkyPolicyId.description: The only daily-sky policy that exists. The calculation service refuses a request naming a policy it does not implement rather than silently answering with the one it has.

localDayResolutionPolicyVersion.description: Version of the closed local-day resolution rule: local noon is the anchor; an ambiguous nominal noon takes the EARLIER offset; a nonexistent noon shifts forward to the first valid instant; a wholly unrepresentable local date is skipped rather than approximated. Changing any of those rules changes reading inputs and therefore changes this version.

anchorResolution.description: How the local-noon anchor was resolved against the pinned IANA database. Recorded in the request identity because a DST-fold day has two defensible anchors and the reading must name which one it used.

dailySkyFactKind.description: Closed launch vocabulary. Stations, eclipses, exact lunations, and seasonal points are deliberately absent: an unimplemented event class silently inferred into a reading is a fact the engine never calculated. The enum order is also the frozen ordering rank.

dailySkyFactId.description: Opaque daily-sky fact handle: 'dsf_' + first 32 lowercase hex of SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 canonical bytes of dailySkyFactIdentityV1. Content-addressed, so the same sky fact carries the same handle in any request, and no handle names a stored row.

factScope.description: Whether a fact involves the reader's own chart. A paragraph supported only by collective facts may not imply the configuration is unique to the reader, and this field is what makes that checkable rather than editorial.

dailySkyErrorClass.description: Deliberately excludes M3's cycle_window_incomplete: a daily-sky scan solves a bounded interval and never has to prove the outer boundaries of an encounter. calculation_failed is the only retryable class; the other three are deterministic refusals that a retry reproduces exactly.

lunarPhaseName.description: Eight closed 45-degree bins centred on 0, 45, 90, 135, 180, 225, 270, and 315 degrees of Sun-to-Moon elongation. Named bins rather than a raw angle because the model may only state a phase that appears in a fact.

aiConsentDataCategory.description: The categories named in the AI-synthesis consent screen, in display order. Every personal section of a provider packet maps to exactly one of these. Adding a category requires a new consent policy version and a fresh grant: a user who agreed to seven categories has not agreed to an eighth.

m5AllowedUse.description: The frozen M0 allowedUse enum narrowed to the lanes M5 may act on. M5 adds no vocabulary: 'daily-reading synthesis' is not an allowed_use, and ai_synthesis is the outer account-level purpose consent, which can never make an otherwise ineligible signal eligible.

readingKeyV5.description: Closed v5 grammar: reading-v5:<user_id>:<YYYY-MM-DD>:r<revision>. The literal namespace makes it disjoint from the legacy 'user:<id>:<date>:<release>:r<n>' grammar under the retained global UNIQUE(reading_key), so a three-value v5 key cannot collide with a four-value legacy one. Stable across command-generation replacement, and never placed in a provider packet.

generationInputId.description: Domain-separated digest of the frozen eligible input and policy — NOT of the prose. The frozen external publisher is nondeterministic whichever transport carries it, so two legitimate deliveries against one command may return different candidates; content_hash and provider_response_hash identify the one that won publication.

contextRef.description: Positional handle for one context item WITHIN one provider packet. Deliberately not a signal id, source id, or consent id: the model never receives a value that survives outside the packet it was built for.

commandReplacementReasonV2.description: Why a terminally failed V2 command was replaced by the next generation. Distinct from M3's set: release_unreadable is impossible on the v5 path, and consent_regranted is operator- or user-initiated rather than automatic. publisher_superseded records a command whose frozen publisher pin names a transport the deployment no longer routes to — it is replaced rather than retried, because nothing about waiting makes it executable, and it is never executed through a different service, which would publish prose that falsifies its own provenance.

reservationReason.description: Which entry point reserved this generation. Recorded because the rollout gate admits entry points one at a time and an audit has to be able to tell a scheduled reservation from a user-triggered one.

publisherProvider.description: The external service that generated the prose. Widened from const 'openai' to this exact enum when Daily moved to the Codex CLI runner: published evidence is never rewritten, so a reading generated under the direct OpenAI transport must still name OpenAI after the routing changed. Deliberately not an open string — an unreviewed processor must not be able to describe itself as the author of a reader's reading. This is the generation SERVICE, not the data processor named on the consent surface.

reasoningEffort.description: Frozen into the command so a configuration change cannot alter an in-flight generation. Production configuration pins 'high'; the other values exist so a frozen older command remains describable.

publisherConfigPin.description: The exact publisher configuration a claimed job must use, frozen at enqueue. Execution passes this to the adapter instead of rereading the current environment: a model or prompt change between enqueue and claim would otherwise silently publish prose the frozen input never described.

aiConsentPin.description: The AI-synthesis grant under which this command was frozen. Consent is rechecked live after the queue claim as well; this pin records what the user had agreed to, and the live recheck decides whether a provider call may happen at all.

categories.description: In the frozen display order. A packet section whose category is absent here cannot be sent.

calculationPin.description: The identity of one frozen calculation exchange. Execution replays the request from the command and recomputes both digests; a changed canonical response is generation_input_id_mismatch, not a newer answer to substitute. Deliberately NOT closed with additionalProperties: both users compose it under allOf and close themselves with unevaluatedProperties, which is the 2020-12 keyword that can see through composition — additionalProperties here would reject the very members those documents add.
